court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Smt. Kamlabai v. Smt. Rukminibai — full case name
facts_of_case: The parties are Smt. Kamlabai, the daughter-in-law of the respondent, and Smt. Rukminibai, the mother-in-law. The petitioner claimed a share in the property left by her husband's father. The trial court allowed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: A testator's intention is the paramount consideration in construing a will.
legal_principles.held: It is well settled that the intention of the testator is the paramount consideration in construing a will. The court must, therefore, try to find out what was the intention of the testator and give effect to it.
cited_cases: Chandrika Prasad Singh v. Union of India, (2011) 2 SCC 764

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the person who seeks to upset the natural meaning of a will.
legal_principles.held: It is well settled that the burden lies on the person who seeks to upset the natural meaning of a will. He must show that the testator did not intend what the words naturally suggest.
cited_cases: Chandrika Prasad Singh v. Union of India, (2011) 2 SCC 764

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the petition was allowed and the respondent was directed to execute the will according to the terms of the will.
